intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Sunrise Temple Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent 12th-century Khmer temple complex at sunrise, wandering through Angkor Wat, Bayon, and Ta Prohm. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver for a full-day guided circuit covering the most iconic temples and hidden gems of the ancient Khmer Empire.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda Visit
experiences.description: Tour the stunning Royal Palace complex and the Silver Pagoda, home to a life-sized gold Buddha studded with diamonds. Explore the surrounding riverside promenade and visit the National Museum of Cambodia to immerse yourself in Khmer art and royal history.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine island of Koh Rong Samloem and spend the day on Saracen Bay, one of Cambodia's most beautiful and tranquil beaches. Snorkel in crystal-clear turquoise waters, spot bioluminescent plankton at night, and enjoy fresh seafood at beachside shacks.
experiences.location: Saracen Bay, Koh Rong Samloem Island

experiences.name: Cambodian Street Food and Market Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening street food walk through the Old Market area, sampling local delicacies such as fish amok, lok lak, nom banh chok noodles, and fresh sugarcane juice. Visit the bustling Phsar Chas night market and learn about the cultural significance of Khmer cuisine from a local guide.

experiences.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and Killing Fields Memorial
experiences.description: Visit the sobering S-21 Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum, a former Khmer Rouge prison, followed by the Choeung Ek Killing Fields memorial. This deeply moving cultural and historical experience provides essential context for understanding modern Cambodian history, resilience, and the country's path to recovery.
experiences.location: Chbar Ampov and Tuol Svay Prey, Phnom Penh

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Once settled, take a leisurely tuk-tuk ride to the nearby Angkor Thom South Gate for a short introductory stroll and first glimpse of the ancient Khmer stone carvings. Grab a local SIM card and exchange currency at a nearby shop.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chaa) area in central Siem Reap to explore the lively night atmosphere. Browse street stalls and soak in the local vibe.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap meal at a local noodle stall near the airport or guesthouse area — try Kuy Teav (rice noodle soup) for around $1–2 USD
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khmer Kitchen Restaurant on Pub Street — authentic Cambodian dishes like Amok fish curry and lok lak for $3–5 USD per dish

day_by_day.notes: Exchange USD at the airport or a local money changer. Cambodia widely accepts USD. Tuk-tuks from the airport to Angkor area cost around $5–8 USD. Negotiate fares in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 5:00 AM) and hire a tuk-tuk to witness the iconic sunrise over Angkor Wat — one of the world's most breathtaking experiences. Spend the morning exploring the main temple complex, including its galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers. Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD) for best value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom — the ancient royal city. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, then walk through the Elephant Terrace and the Terrace of the Leper King. Explore the Baphuon temple pyramid.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the guesthouse to freshen up, then head to the Night Market (Angkor Night Market) for cheap shopping and cultural performances. Enjoy a $1 USD beer and street snacks.

meals.breakfast: Light snack from a street vendor near Angkor Wat — banana pancakes or sticky rice for $1 USD
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Angkor Thom — try a Khmer set meal (rice, vegetable stir-fry, soup) for $3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Street food at Angkor Night Market — grilled corn, spring rolls, and fresh fruit shakes for under $5 USD total

day_by_day.notes: Bring plenty of water and sunscreen — November is generally dry and warm (around 28–32°C). Wear modest clothing (covered shoulders and knees) to enter temple complexes. A tuk-tuk day hire costs around $12–15 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ta Prohm — the iconic 'Tomb Raider' temple famously engulfed by massive tree roots. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Explore the atmospheric jungle ruins and photograph the stunning silk-cotton and strangler fig trees intertwined with ancient stone walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Banteay Srei — a smaller but exquisitely carved 10th-century temple about 25 km from Siem Reap, known as the 'Citadel of Women' for its intricate pink sandstone carvings. Afterward, stop at the Landmine Museum nearby to learn about Cambodia's tragic history with landmines and ongoing demining efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Apsara Arts Association or catch a free traditional Apsara dance performance at a local restaurant. Explore the Alley West area near Pub Street for budget bars and local hangouts.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse or a nearby café — Khmer-style fried rice with egg for $2 USD
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant en route to Banteay Srei — grilled chicken with rice and fresh coconut for $3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Dinner at Singing Tree Café — a budget-friendly vegetarian-friendly spot with Khmer and Western options for $4–6 USD

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires a longer tuk-tuk journey — negotiate a full-day tuk-tuk hire ($15–18 USD) to cover both sites efficiently. The Landmine Museum charges a small donation-based entry fee.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Preah Khan Temple — a sprawling complex of corridors, courtyards, and shrines dedicated to the father of King Jayavarman VII. Less crowded than Angkor Wat, it offers an authentic jungle-temple experience. Continue to Neak Pean — an artificial island temple set in the middle of a sacred pond.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the East Mebon and Pre Rup temples — two pyramid-style temple mountains offering panoramic views of the surrounding countryside. Pre Rup is especially beautiful in the late afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Take a sunset boat trip on Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Witness the floating villages and stunning orange sunset over the water. Boat tours cost around $10–15 USD per person.

meals.breakfast: Fresh baguette with butter and coffee at a local bakery — a French colonial legacy in Cambodia — for $1.50 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a market stall — rice and grilled fish wrapped in banana leaves for $2–3 USD
meals.dinner: Fish Amok (Cambodia's national dish) at a lakeside restaurant near Tonlé Sap — $4–5 USD

day_by_day.notes: Tonlé Sap Lake is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. November is the end of the rainy season, so water levels are high — ideal for boat tours. Negotiate boat prices at the dock and go with a local operator for the best rates.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning cooking class at a local Siem Reap cooking school (around $15–20 USD). Learn to prepare traditional Khmer dishes like Fish Amok, green mango salad, and lok lak. Many classes include a market visit to source fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum ($12 USD entry) to deepen your understanding of Khmer history, art, and civilization. The museum's multimedia exhibits provide excellent context for the temples already visited. Afterward, stroll through the French Quarter to admire colonial architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Siem Reap Art Center Night Market — a more local-focused alternative to the main night market, featuring handmade crafts, silk scarves, and Cambodian artwork at reasonable prices. Catch a shadow puppet show if available.

meals.breakfast: Included in cooking class market visit, or grab a $1 USD coconut and banana from a street cart
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you cooked in the morning class!
meals.dinner: Rooftop dining at a budget guesthouse restaurant — Khmer BBQ (grilled meats and vegetables on a tabletop grill) for $6–8 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance online or through your guesthouse. This is a great cultural immersion activity and the skills learned are a wonderful souvenir. Check for free or donation-based shadow puppet performances at local NGO centers.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap by bus to Phnom Penh — Cambodia's capital city. Take a budget express bus (Giant Ibis or Mekong Express — around $9–12 USD, approximately 5–6 hours). Depart by 7:00–8:00 AM to arrive by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to a budget guesthouse near the riverfront (dorms from $5 USD, private rooms from $12–15 USD). Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda ($10 USD entry) — a stunning complex of royal buildings, golden spires, and the famous Emerald Buddha. Dress modestly.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sisowath Quay (Phnom Penh Riverfront) as the sun sets over the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers. Browse the riverside night market and enjoy the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Snack on the bus or grab a quick $1 USD baguette sandwich before departure from Siem Reap
meals.lunch: Bus stop break or street food upon arrival in Phnom Penh — Bai Sach Chrouk (pork and rice) for $1.50–2 USD
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — a social enterprise training at-risk youth in hospitality; great tapas-style Khmer food for $4–7 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets in advance during peak season. Giant Ibis is highly recommended for safety and reliability. Store luggage at the bus terminal or guesthouse if arriving before check-in time.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply moving and historically essential site documenting the Khmer Rouge's atrocities between 1975–1979. Entry is $5 USD. Hire an audio guide or a survivor guide for deeper insight. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial ($6 USD entry with audio guide) — located about 15 km from the city center. This UNESCO-listed memorial is one of the most important historical sites in Southeast Asia and provides crucial context to Cambodia's modern history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and visit the Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a grand Art Deco building housing hundreds of stalls selling jewelry, clothing, and local goods. Unwind with a sunset drink at a riverside bar.

meals.breakfast: Num Banh Chok (Khmer rice noodles with green curry sauce) from a local market stall — $1–1.50 USD
meals.lunch: Simple lunch near Tuol Sleng — local rice and curry at a nearby eatery for $2–3 USD
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant — another social enterprise specializing in traditional Cambodian cuisine including deep-fried tarantulas (adventurous!) and classic dishes for $5–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: These sites are emotionally heavy. Take breaks as needed and approach with respect and sensitivity. Photography rules are strictly enforced at both sites. Tuk-tuk to Choeung Ek and back costs around $8–10 USD round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phnom Penh early by bus or shared taxi to Sihanoukville (approximately 4–5 hours, $8–10 USD by bus). From Sihanoukville, take a ferry to Koh Rong Sanloem — a stunning island with pristine beaches and a relaxed backpacker vibe. Ferry costs around $25 USD round trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Rong Sanloem and check in to a budget beach bungalow or guesthouse on Saracen Bay or Lazy Beach (from $15–25 USD per night). Spend the afternoon relaxing on the white sand beach, swimming in crystal-clear turquoise water, and snorkeling around nearby reefs.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach and look for bioluminescent plankton after dark — Koh Rong Sanloem is famous for this magical natural phenomenon. Take a night swim to see the glowing blue water.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before boarding the bus in Phnom Penh — $1–2 USD street food
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry or grab food upon arrival — fresh coconut and fruit from a beach vendor for $2 USD
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood BBQ dinner at a beachside restaurant on Saracen Bay — grilled fish, prawns, and squid with rice for $6–10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance during peak season (November–February). Koh Rong Sanloem has limited ATMs — bring sufficient USD cash. Electricity may be limited to certain hours on the island. Bring insect repellent for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day on Koh Rong Sanloem. Join a guided snorkeling trip to nearby coral reefs (around $10–15 USD per person) to see colorful fish, sea turtles, and vibrant marine life. Alternatively, rent a kayak ($5–8 USD per hour) and paddle around the island's coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike across the island through the jungle trail to Lazy Beach — a secluded and beautiful beach on the western side of the island. The trail takes about 30–45 minutes through dense tropical forest. Relax and swim at this quieter beach before heading back.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final evening on the island. Join other travelers at a beachside bonfire or bar. Try a Cambodian rum cocktail (Samai Rum is a local brand) and stargaze on the beach away from light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — eggs, toast, and fresh fruit for $2–3 USD
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Lazy Beach — simple Khmer fried rice or sandwich for $3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Dinner at a different beachfront restaurant — try Khmer red curry with vegetables and rice for $4–5 USD; finish with a fresh fruit smoothie

day_by_day.notes: Wear reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem. The jungle trail to Lazy Beach can be muddy — wear appropriate footwear. Confirm your return ferry schedule for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up for a final sunrise on the beach. Take a morning swim and pack up your belongings. Board the morning ferry back to Sihanoukville (check schedule — usually departs around 8:00–9:00 AM). From Sihanoukville, arrange onward transport back to Phnom Penh or directly to the airport depending on your departure flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time permits before departure, explore Sihanoukville's Otres Beach area — a quieter and more laid-back alternative to the main town beach. Pick up last-minute souvenirs such as silk scarves, carved wooden items, or Kampot pepper at a local market.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on flight schedule — head to Phnom Penh International Airport or relax at a café. Reflect on an incredible 10-day journey through Cambodia's history, culture, and natural beauty.

meals.breakfast: Final island breakfast — fresh fruit bowl and coffee at your guesthouse for $2–3 USD
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sihanoukville — Khmer noodle soup or grilled skewers from a street stall for $2–3 USD
meals.dinner: Airport meal or a farewell dinner in Phnom Penh — try a final bowl of Samlor Korko (Khmer vegetable and pork stew) for $3–4 USD

day_by_day.notes: Confirm all transport connections and flight details the night before. Keep $25 USD aside for departure tax if not included in your ticket (most modern tickets include it). Exchange remaining Cambodian Riel back to USD before leaving. Total estimated budget for the full 10-day trip: $350–500 USD including accommodation, transport, food, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange a tuk-tuk or pre-booked transfer to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the hotel grounds to orient yourself. Visit the nearby Angkor National Museum (about 15 minutes by tuk-tuk) for a 2-hour introductory overview of Khmer civilization — perfect preparation for the temple visits ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Siem Reap's famous Pub Street and Old Market (Psar Chas) area for a gentle evening walk. Browse the night market stalls and soak in the vibrant atmosphere of the town center.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a café near the hotel upon arrival — try a bowl of Khmer noodle soup (Kuy Teav) at a local eatery for around $3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak or Mahob Restaurant near Old Market — mid-range Khmer cuisine with dishes like fish amok and lok lak, budget $10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to Khmer Riel at the airport or a local exchange booth. USD is widely accepted in Cambodia. Arrange a tuk-tuk driver for the next few days — a reliable driver for temple visits typically costs $15–20/day.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early (4:30 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise. Watch the temple's reflection shimmer in the reflecting pools as dawn breaks — one of Southeast Asia's most breathtaking spectacles. Spend the morning (until ~10:00 AM) exploring Angkor Wat's galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers. Hire a licensed guide at the entrance ($20–25) for deeper historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a mid-morning snack break, visit the South Gate of Angkor Thom and explore the magnificent Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces. Continue to the Baphuon Temple and the Elephant Terrace within the Angkor Thom complex. Take a shaded rest break between 12:00–13:30 to avoid peak heat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your hotel to rest and shower. Head out to Siem Reap's Alley West for dinner, then explore the night market for handmade crafts and silk scarves as souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks and water from a convenience store the night before for the early sunrise visit. Grab a proper breakfast at a café near the Angkor Wat entrance after sunrise — rice porridge (Bobor) or a baguette with egg, $2–4
meals.lunch: Lunch at one of the open-air restaurants near Angkor Thom's south gate — try a Khmer curry or fried rice, $5–8
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mie Café or Sugar Palm Restaurant in Siem Reap town — authentic Khmer dishes, $10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Angkor Archaeological Park pass before sunset the day prior if possible (3-day pass: $62, 1-day: $37). Bring sunscreen, a hat, and at least 1.5 liters of water. Dress modestly — shoulders and knees must be covered to enter the temples.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the atmospheric jungle temple of Ta Prohm — famous for its massive strangler fig and silk-cotton trees growing through the stone ruins, and a filming location for Tomb Raider. Arrive early (7:00 AM) before tour groups arrive. Spend 1.5–2 hours wandering the moss-covered corridors and collapsed galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Kdei and the serene Sra Srang reservoir (Royal Bathing Pool) nearby. In the late afternoon, travel to Banteay Srei Temple (~35 km north of Siem Reap) — a 10th-century masterpiece carved in pink sandstone with extraordinarily intricate detail, considered the jewel of Khmer art.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Apsara dance performance at Angkor Village Theatre or Smile of Angkor — a culturally immersive evening showcasing classical Khmer dance and music. Tickets typically include dinner ($25–35 per person).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel's restaurant or a nearby café — Khmer-style eggs and fresh tropical fruit, $4–6
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a local food stall near Ta Prohm — rice with grilled meats or noodles, $3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner included with the Apsara dance performance, or dine at Viroth's Restaurant for refined Cambodian cuisine, $12–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Banteay Srei takes about 45 minutes by tuk-tuk. Consider upgrading to an air-conditioned car for this longer excursion ($30–40 for the day). Banteay Srei is best photographed in the afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the lesser-known but stunning Preah Khan Temple — a sprawling 12th-century monastic complex dedicated to Jayavarman VII's father. Wander its long colonnaded corridors and moss-draped courtyards with far fewer tourists. Nearby, explore Neak Pean, an artificial island temple built on a circular pond, accessible via a boardwalk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the remote Beng Mealea Temple (~70 km east of Siem Reap) — an unrestored jungle temple completely consumed by vegetation. Wooden walkways guide you through collapsed towers and root-entangled stones. This is one of Cambodia's most adventurous and atmospheric temple experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap and enjoy a relaxed evening. Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop showroom (free entry) to learn about traditional Khmer silk weaving and stone carving crafts, and pick up ethically made souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — fresh fruit, eggs, and Cambodian coffee (strong with condensed milk), $4–6
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Beng Mealea village — simple Khmer rice dishes, $3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner at Siem Reap's Kandal Village area — try Miss Wong (cocktail bar with Asian tapas) or Haven Restaurant (social enterprise training Cambodian youth), $10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Beng Mealea requires a separate entry fee (~$5). Hire a car rather than a tuk-tuk for this day as the roads are longer. The round trip takes approximately 3–4 hours of driving total. Wear closed-toe shoes for Beng Mealea as the terrain is uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Visit a floating village (Kompong Khleang is more authentic and less touristy than Chong Kneas) to see how thousands of Cambodians live on water, observe floating schools, and witness the unique ecosystem. Boat tours depart around 7:30–8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap by early afternoon. Visit the Cambodian Cultural Village for a condensed overview of Cambodia's ethnic groups, traditional architecture, and folk performances — good for cultural context.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Khmer cooking class in the evening (several operators offer 3-hour evening classes for $25–35). Learn to prepare fish amok, green mango salad, and Khmer red curry — and eat your creations for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the boat tour — rice porridge or toast with fruit, $4–5
meals.lunch: Lunch at a floating restaurant on Tonlé Sap Lake — fresh river fish dishes, $6–10
meals.dinner: Your own cooking class creations! Alternatively, dine at Malis Restaurant for upscale Cambodian cuisine, $15–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Tonlé Sap Lake boat tour costs approximately $15–25 per person. The water level in November is still relatively high, making it an excellent time to visit the floating villages. Bring insect repellent for the lake excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap early by bus or private transfer to Phnom Penh (approximately 5.5–6 hours by road, or 1 hour by domestic flight). The bus journey with Mekong Express or Giant Ibis offers comfortable air-conditioned coaches at $12–15. If flying, budget $50–80. Use the journey to rest and enjoy the Cambodian countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check into a mid-range hotel near the riverside (Sisowath Quay area). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and the Silver Pagoda — a stunning complex of royal buildings and Buddhist temples. The Silver Pagoda floor is tiled with 5,000 silver tiles and houses priceless Buddha statues.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the lively Sisowath Quay riverside promenade as the sun sets over the Mekong and Tonlé Sap confluence. Browse the evening street food vendors and enjoy the city's energy.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel in Siem Reap before departure, $4–6
meals.lunch: Lunch stop en route to Phnom Penh at a local roadside restaurant (bus companies typically stop at a designated rest area), $4–6
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant (Phnom Penh social enterprise in a colonial villa, famous for Cambodian countryside cuisine) — $12–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book your bus or flight from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh in advance. Giant Ibis is highly recommended for safety and comfort. The Royal Palace closes at 11:00 AM–2:00 PM for lunch, so plan your afternoon visit after 2:00 PM. Dress code applies — shoulders and knees covered.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school converted into a Khmer Rouge detention and torture center. This deeply moving and important museum provides crucial historical understanding of Cambodia's tragic recent past. Allow 2–2.5 hours. A guided tour ($6–8) is strongly recommended for context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel 15 km south of Phnom Penh to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial — the most significant of Cambodia's killing fields, now a peaceful memorial with a Buddhist stupa containing skulls of victims. Audio guides are available and highly recommended ($3). Return to Phnom Penh and visit the National Museum of Cambodia, housing the world's largest collection of Khmer art and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco building from 1937 — for evening browsing and souvenir shopping. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the Mekong.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a riverside café — French baguette with pâté (a colonial legacy) or Cambodian noodles, $3–5
meals.lunch: Lunch near Tuol Sleng at a local Khmer restaurant — a light meal given the emotional morning, $5–8
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends Restaurant (Phnom Penh) — a social enterprise training street youth in hospitality, excellent tapas-style Cambodian fusion, $10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy. Take your time and allow space for reflection. These sites are essential for understanding Cambodia's history but can be distressing. Entry to Tuol Sleng: $5; Choeung Ek: $6. Tuk-tuk to Choeung Ek costs about $8–10 round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phnom Penh early by bus or minivan to Sihanoukville (approximately 4 hours), then take a 45-minute ferry to Koh Rong Samloem — one of Cambodia's most beautiful and unspoiled islands. The island has pristine white-sand beaches, crystal-clear turquoise water, and a relaxed atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a mid-range beach bungalow on Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay. Spend the afternoon unwinding on the beach, swimming in the warm Gulf of Thailand waters, and snorkeling around the coral reefs just offshore. Rent snorkeling gear from your guesthouse ($5–8).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the spectacular bioluminescent plankton light up the shallow waters after dark — a magical natural phenomenon best seen on moonless nights in November. Enjoy a beachside dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel in Phnom Penh before departure, $4–6
meals.lunch: Lunch on the ferry or at a beach shack upon arrival on the island — fresh grilled fish, $6–10
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant on Saracen Bay — grilled seafood platter with rice and vegetables, $10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets from Sihanoukville to Koh Rong Samloem cost approximately $20–25 round trip. Book accommodation on the island in advance as options are limited. Bring cash as ATMs are unavailable on the island. November weather is generally good for the southern coast — dry season is beginning.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise walk along the deserted beach. Join a guided jungle trek through the island's interior rainforest to discover tropical wildlife, rare birds, and hidden waterfalls. Treks are organized by most guesthouses ($10–15 per person, 2–3 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip around the island to snorkel at remote coral reef spots with abundant marine life — colorful fish, sea turtles, and vibrant corals. Boat trips typically include 2–3 snorkeling stops and cost $15–20 per person. Alternatively, kayak around the island's coastline and explore hidden coves.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the last island evening relaxing in a hammock on the beach with a cocktail. Enjoy a final beachside dinner with freshly caught seafood and reflect on the journey. Watch the stars from the beach — with minimal light pollution, the night sky is extraordinary.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit platter and eggs at your beachside bungalow, $4–6
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the boat during the snorkeling trip, or a beach shack lunch on return — $5–8
meals.dinner: Dinner at your guesthouse restaurant or a neighboring beach bar — lobster or king prawn with garlic butter, $12–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen only when snorkeling to protect the coral ecosystems. Respect the island's fragile environment — no plastic bags or single-use plastics. The island has limited electricity (often generator-powered), so charge devices when possible.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast on the beach as the sun rises over the Gulf of Thailand. Take a last swim or peaceful walk along the shoreline. Pack up and check out of your beach bungalow. Catch the morning ferry back to Sihanoukville (departures typically at 8:00 AM or 11:00 AM — confirm with your guesthouse).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Sihanoukville and arrange onward transport to Phnom Penh International Airport (4-hour drive) or Sihanoukville Airport for domestic connections. If time permits before your flight, browse Sihanoukville's Victory Beach briefly or pick up last-minute souvenirs. Reflect on 10 incredible days exploring Cambodia's temples, culture, and coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final beach breakfast — fresh tropical fruits, pancakes, and Cambodian coffee, $4–6
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Sihanoukville before onward travel — local Khmer noodles or a sandwich, $4–7
meals.dinner: Airport meal or meal on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm ferry and transport schedules the night before. Allow at least 3–3.5 hours from Sihanoukville to Phnom Penh Airport, plus 2 hours for check-in. Consider purchasing a small bag of Kampot pepper, Cambodian coffee, or handwoven silk as final souvenirs — all available at Phnom Penh Airport duty-free.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to your boutique stay within Angkor Archaeological Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in and settle into your boutique property. After freshening up, enjoy a leisurely orientation walk through the hotel grounds and surrounding temple periphery. Visit the nearby Angkor Conservation compound for a first glimpse of ancient stone carvings in a relaxed, uncrowded setting. Stop by the hotel's infinity pool for a refreshing swim as you acclimate.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at your hotel's signature restaurant or a short transfer to Cuisine Wat Damnak — one of Siem Reap's most celebrated fine-dining establishments offering a modern Cambodian tasting menu with seasonal, locally sourced ingredients. Pair with a curated Cambodian craft cocktail or wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments and afternoon tea arranged by the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak — modern Khmer tasting menu (6 courses), or hotel signature dining with Cambodian-French fusion cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-in confirmation in advance. Ask the concierge to brief you on temple pass options (1-day, 3-day, or 7-day Angkor Pass) and purchase the appropriate pass this evening or first thing tomorrow morning to maximize temple time.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise experience — one of the world's most breathtaking spectacles. Arrive at the reflecting pool by 05:30 with a private guide. As the sun rises over the five towers, your guide narrates the temple's 12th-century Khmer history and Hindu-Buddhist iconography. Explore the outer galleries featuring the stunning bas-relief of the Churning of the Ocean of Milk (nearly 50 meters long) with expert commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the walled city of Angkor Thom, including the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon pyramid temple, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Take a private tuk-tuk or air-conditioned vehicle between sites. Return to the hotel for a midday rest and pool time during peak heat hours (12:00–14:30).
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the hotel terrace. Dinner at Malis Restaurant in Siem Reap — an upscale celebration of authentic Khmer royal cuisine in an elegant garden setting. Try the Fish Amok (national dish) and Khmer-style beef lok lak.

meals.breakfast: Pre-sunrise light breakfast box prepared by the hotel (coffee, pastries, tropical fruit) taken at Angkor Wat
meals.lunch: Elegant poolside lunch at the hotel — fresh spring rolls, grilled fish, coconut soup, and cold-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Malis Restaurant — Khmer royal cuisine in a refined open-air garden setting

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and bring a sarong (required to enter some temple areas). Sunrise at Angkor Wat in November is typically around 06:00. Mosquito repellent and sun protection are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Ta Prohm — the atmospheric 'Tomb Raider' temple famously engulfed by giant silk-cotton and strangler fig trees. Arrive early (07:00) to beat the crowds. Your guide will explain the Jayavarman VII-era monastery history and point out rare carvings. Continue to the elegant Banteay Kdei and the sacred Srah Srang reservoir, a royal bathing pool with a stunning lakeside terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Srei ('Citadel of Women') — a 10th-century temple renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest example of classical Khmer art. Located 25 km north of Angkor, this is best visited by private air-conditioned vehicle. Stop at the Landmine Museum en route for a sobering but important cultural experience. Return to the hotel for a spa treatment — book a traditional Khmer herbal compress massage or a full aromatherapy body ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Private dinner experience: arrange a candlelit dinner within a temple courtyard (some luxury hotels offer exclusive after-hours temple dining experiences with special permits) or dine at Shinta Mani's acclaimed restaurant for a farm-to-table Cambodian menu.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the hotel — Cambodian congee (borbor), tropical fruit platter, eggs Benedict, freshly brewed Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style luxury lunch arranged by the hotel, enjoyed near Srah Srang reservoir under a shaded pavilion
meals.dinner: Exclusive private temple dinner (hotel-arranged) or Shinta Mani Restaurant — contemporary Cambodian farm-to-table cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is a must-see but requires a 45-minute drive — best done in a private air-conditioned car. Photography at Ta Prohm is spectacular in morning light. Book spa treatments in advance as slots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hot air balloon flight over the Angkor Archaeological Park — a truly premium experience offering sweeping aerial views of Angkor Wat, the jungle canopy, and the distant Tonlé Sap Lake. Flights typically last 30–45 minutes and depart around 06:00. Alternatively, take a private helicopter tour for an even more exclusive perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the lesser-visited outer temples on the Grand Circuit: Preah Khan (a massive monastic complex with beautiful tree-root encroachments), Neak Pean (an artificial island temple with a unique circular design), and Ta Som (a small but perfectly preserved temple). Enjoy the tranquility of these less-crowded gems with your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an exclusive Apsara dance performance — the classical court dance of Cambodia, a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. Opt for a private performance arranged at your hotel or at the Angkor Village Theatre for a more intimate setting. Follow with dinner at The Sugar Palm — a beloved Siem Reap restaurant specializing in traditional family recipes.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-flight snack (coffee, fruit, pastries) before balloon; full breakfast at hotel upon return
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional Khmer family home arranged through the hotel — an authentic cultural dining experience with home-cooked Cambodian dishes
meals.dinner: The Sugar Palm — traditional Khmer recipes including kroeung-based curries and smoked fish dishes, followed by Apsara performance

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon flights are weather-dependent — confirm availability the night before. Book Apsara performance tickets at least 48 hours in advance. The Grand Circuit temples are best explored in a private tuk-tuk or car for flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Koh Ker — an ancient remote capital 120 km northeast of Siem Reap, featuring the dramatic seven-tiered Prasat Thom pyramid temple rising 36 meters above the jungle. Travel by private vehicle (approximately 2 hours). The site is remarkably uncrowded and offers an Indiana Jones-style adventure. Explore the 30+ temple structures scattered across the jungle with your private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Beng Mealea on the return journey — a sprawling 12th-century temple largely consumed by jungle, with no restoration, offering a raw and authentic experience. Wander through collapsed galleries, overgrown courtyards, and moss-covered towers. Return to Siem Reap by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel — enjoy the pool or book an in-room couples' spa treatment. Dinner at Mahob Restaurant — a refined Cambodian dining experience in a beautifully restored colonial villa, with an emphasis on heritage recipes and premium local ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — fresh fruit, Cambodian noodle soup (kuy teav), pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch prepared by the hotel, enjoyed at Koh Ker under the shade of ancient trees
meals.dinner: Mahob Restaurant — heritage Cambodian cuisine in a colonial villa setting with excellent wine list

day_by_day.notes: Koh Ker and Beng Mealea require a full day — depart by 07:00. Roads are paved but long; ensure the vehicle has air conditioning and water. Wear sturdy shoes for Beng Mealea as the terrain is uneven. These sites require separate entry fees in addition to the Angkor Pass.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat tour on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Depart from Chong Kneas or the more exclusive Kompong Khleang floating village (less touristy). Observe the extraordinary floating villages, stilted houses, floating schools, and fish farms. Your private guide explains the unique ecosystem and the lives of the lake's 1.2 million residents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique — a social enterprise training disadvantaged Cambodians in traditional silk weaving, stone carving, lacquerware, and silversmithing. Watch artisans at work and select premium handcrafted souvenirs. Continue to the Angkor National Museum for a world-class multimedia journey through Khmer civilization — the Hall of a Thousand Buddhas is particularly impressive.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at Miss Wong — a glamorous 1920s Shanghai-inspired speakeasy bar in Siem Reap's Pub Street area. Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak for a return visit or try Spoons Restaurant — a social enterprise fine-dining experience training at-risk youth in culinary arts.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Cambodian-style pork porridge, tropical fruit, fresh juices, and French press coffee
meals.lunch: Floating restaurant lunch on Tonlé Sap Lake — fresh river fish, steamed rice, morning glory stir-fry, and local beer
meals.dinner: Spoons Restaurant — contemporary Cambodian cuisine with a social mission; excellent cocktail pairing menu

day_by_day.notes: Tonlé Sap Lake water levels are highest in November (post-monsoon), making it the most spectacular time to visit. Kompong Khleang is 60 km from Siem Reap but far more authentic than Chong Kneas — worth the extra travel time. Bring sunscreen and a hat for the boat tour.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Siem Reap airport for a short domestic flight to Sihanoukville (or Koh Kong), then onward by private speedboat to Koh Rong Samloem — Cambodia's most pristine and exclusive island. Check in to a luxury eco-resort such as Song Saa Private Island or Koh Rong Samloem's Song Saa for an overwater villa or beachfront suite experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: First afternoon on the island — settle in, explore the resort's private beach, and snorkel the crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and coral. The island's Saracen Bay offers some of the most tranquil turquoise waters in Southeast Asia. Optional: kayaking or paddleboarding through the mangrove channels.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the beach as the sun dips into the Gulf of Thailand. Private beach bonfire dinner — fresh grilled seafood (lobster, tiger prawns, barramundi), tropical salads, and Cambodian coconut desserts under a sky full of stars.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast in Siem Reap before departure — full buffet spread
meals.lunch: In-flight snack or light arrival lunch at the island resort — fresh coconut, tropical fruit platter, grilled fish
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire dinner — whole grilled lobster, tiger prawns, fresh catches of the day with Cambodian spice rubs and dipping sauces

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flights and speedboat transfers well in advance. Song Saa Private Island is one of Cambodia's most exclusive properties — reservations should be made months ahead. Pack reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem. November weather on the coast is generally excellent — dry season begins.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkeling or diving excursion to the nearby marine reserve — the waters around Koh Rong Samloem are home to seahorses, reef sharks, rays, and vibrant coral gardens. A private dive guide accompanies you. Non-divers can enjoy a glass-bottom boat tour over the reef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island on foot via jungle trails to hidden beaches — M'Pai Bay on the northern tip offers a secluded, undeveloped stretch of white sand accessible only by a 45-minute jungle hike or short boat ride. Spend the afternoon in complete seclusion. Return to the resort for a beachside spa treatment — traditional Khmer herbal wrap and deep tissue massage in an open-air pavilion overlooking the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga session on the beach with a private instructor. Dinner at the resort's overwater restaurant — a refined seafood and Cambodian menu with curated wine pairings. Try the Kampot pepper crab — a Cambodian delicacy using the world-renowned Kampot pepper.

meals.breakfast: Tropical breakfast delivered to your villa terrace — fresh papaya, dragon fruit, Cambodian banana pancakes, cold-brew coffee, and fresh coconut water
meals.lunch: Beach picnic at M'Pai Bay — gourmet hamper prepared by the resort with sandwiches, tropical fruits, artisan cheeses, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Resort overwater restaurant — Kampot pepper crab, grilled sea bass with lemongrass, coconut panna cotta, premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Bioluminescent plankton can sometimes be seen in the waters around Koh Rong Samloem at night (November is a good month) — ask the resort to arrange a night swimming experience. Diving certification is required for scuba; snorkeling is available to all.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning — sleep in, enjoy breakfast on your villa terrace, and take a final swim in the resort's infinity pool overlooking the ocean. Optional: morning fishing excursion with local fishermen, then have your catch prepared by the resort chef for lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat transfer to the mainland and onward to Kampot — a charming French colonial riverside town 3 hours from Sihanoukville. Check in to a boutique luxury guesthouse such as Knai Bang Chatt (a stunning modernist villa resort on the Kampot River). Explore Kampot's atmospheric old town on foot or by cyclo — admire the French colonial architecture, visit the durian market, and stroll along the riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Kampot River aboard a private wooden boat — drift past mangroves, fishing villages, and the dramatic Bokor Mountain silhouette as the sky turns golden. Dinner at Knai Bang Chatt's acclaimed Sailing Club restaurant — contemporary Cambodian cuisine with a strong emphasis on locally sourced Kampot pepper and fresh river seafood.

meals.breakfast: Tropical villa breakfast on your private terrace — Cambodian rice porridge, exotic fruit, pastries, and freshly brewed Cambodian robusta coffee
meals.lunch: Freshly caught fish lunch at the island resort, prepared to order by the resort chef
meals.dinner: Knai Bang Chatt Sailing Club — Kampot river prawns with black pepper, amok fish curry, lychee sorbet; riverside setting

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is famous for its pepper plantations — book a private pepper farm tour for the next morning. Knai Bang Chatt is one of Cambodia's most architecturally stunning boutique hotels — request a river-view room. The drive from Sihanoukville to Kampot takes approximately 1.5 hours by private car.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of a Kampot pepper plantation — visit one of the world's most prestigious pepper farms (Sothy's Pepper Farm or La Plantation) to learn about the cultivation, harvesting, and processing of Kampot's UNESCO Geographical Indication-protected pepper. Taste the different varieties (red, black, white, and green) and purchase premium pepper to take home. Continue to the dramatic Bokor Hill Station — a 1920s French colonial ghost town perched 1,080 meters above sea level, featuring an abandoned casino, church, and palace shrouded in mist.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Kampot for a final Cambodian lunch. Private transfer to Phnom Penh (approximately 3 hours by car) for departure preparations. If time allows, stop at the Phnom Penh riverfront for a brief stroll along the Sisowath Quay promenade, visit the Royal Palace exterior, and browse the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Phnom Penh at Malis Phnom Penh — the capital branch of Cambodia's finest restaurant, serving royal Khmer cuisine in an elegant garden setting. Transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport for departure, or overnight in Phnom Penh if the flight departs the following day.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Knai Bang Chatt — eggs your way, Cambodian noodle soup, tropical fruit, and Kampot coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch in Kampot at Rikitikitavi — a beloved riverside restaurant with excellent Cambodian and international dishes; try the fish curry and fresh spring rolls
meals.dinner: Malis Phnom Penh — royal Khmer tasting menu, Cambodian craft cocktails, and a curated dessert selection; perfect farewell to Cambodia

day_by_day.notes: La Plantation pepper farm offers excellent guided tours with advance booking. Bokor Mountain can be foggy and cool — bring a light jacket. Allow at least 3 hours for the Kampot–Phnom Penh drive. Confirm flight departure times and arrange airport transfer through the hotel concierge. Purchase Kampot pepper, Artisans Angkor crafts, and Cambodian silk as premium souvenirs.
